title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I take this opportunity to let thee know how and where we are by John Shoemaker, who we expect will be here this evening in order to attend Pelham Monthly meeting which is tomorrow, & return homewards pretty soon. I expect now have gotten received a letter from Martha dated about two weeks back at Genesee River. We got to Black Creek settlement last fifth day, was a week left there on second day morning. Got to Pelham in the evening. We were at the falls of Niagara between Black Creek & Pelham it was a very grand sight, a great body of water a great deal larger than Delaware that falls 150 feet perpendicular. We have had our health very well for the most part since we left home. Riding agrees with me very well, & mother stands it quite as well as she expected very often think of thee and the rest of you, and hope in about 5 weeks to see you, but you must you must not be disappointed if we stay a week longer. We expect to set off on fifth day morning for Young Street, 3 days journey on a bad road. We think it likely we shall be about two weeks gone till we return here again. & then we

closer.salute: Not having anything more in particular to write, I conclude in love to you all and Uncle William’s family in which mother joins me– and reman thy affectionate Brother

postscript.p: PS Please to let grandmother Evans know how we are if you have any opportunity
